comparison: Perfect alignment on body size decrease trends (C8, C9, C33, C36, C39, C57, C58, C71). Both evaluations support the finding that titanosauriformes showed a decrease in body size with strong phylogenetic signal, violating Cope's rule. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as supporting previous findings despite nuanced statistical results.

Strong overlap on morphological trends and phylogenetic signal (C2, C4, C32, C37, C38, C42, C64, C68). Both evaluations support the shape-change trends along PC axes with significant phylogenetic signals. Peer reviewers describe these findings as 'convincing' and providing 'new information.' OpenEval R2 also includes claims about wide-gauge posture (C27, C28) that peer R1 touches on through C41, C63.

Strong agreement on decoupling of posture from body size (C6, C34, C35, C45, C59, C70). Both evaluations support the finding that wide-gauge posture was not significantly correlated with gigantism within Titanosauria. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a key finding. Peer R2 also includes exaptation claims (C7, C69) and morphological variation (C62, C66).

Partial overlap on exaptation interpretation (C7, C69). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting that while decoupling is well-supported, the exaptation scenario requires more evidence. Peer reviewers support the broader interpretation about posture-size decoupling but do not specifically evaluate the exaptation claim's strength.

Agreement on convergent evolution findings (C5, C40, C73). Both evaluations support the interpretation that lack of significant differences between subclades reflects convergent evolution. Peer R3 also includes functional/biomechanical interpretations (C51, C54, C72, C74, C75) that OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

Overlap on functional interpretations (C47-C49, C51, C74, C75). OpenEval rates these biomechanical and functional hypotheses as UNCERTAIN, noting they are plausible but speculative without direct testing. Peer reviewers acknowledge these suggestions about biomechanical factors and convergence as part of the study's contribution without expressing reservations.

Agreement on methodological approach (C22, C23, C76, C77, C78). Both evaluations support the PCA methodology and geometric morphometric analyses. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 3D geometric morphometric approach as providing new information. Peer R5 also covers statistical methods (C79, C81-C84) that OpenEval addresses in R11 and R14.

Agreement on statistical methodology (C81-C84). Both evaluations support the phylogenetic comparative methods as appropriate and well-applied. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment while peer reviewers praise the overall analytical approach.

Partial overlap on centroid size proxy (C79, C80). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the proxy is reasonable but indirect and introduces uncertainty. Peer R7 addresses background claims (C1, C10-C13) that OpenEval covers in R16, without specifically evaluating the centroid size methodology.

Strong agreement on background/contextual claims (C1, C10, C11, C12, C13). Both evaluations support these foundational premises about sauropod biology as well-established knowledge with appropriate citations.

Partial overlap on wide-gauge posture interpretation (C41, C63). OpenEval supports the interpretation that PC results reflect wide-gauge posture evolution. Peer R1 includes these claims within broader support for morphological trends and phylogenetic signals.

Agreement on morphological variability within titanosaurs (C60, C61, C65). Both evaluations support observations of shape-change trends and variability within subclades. Peer reviewers note these trends as 'interesting' even where statistical significance was not achieved.

Partial overlap on PC2 findings (C30, C50). OpenEval supports the lack of phylogenetic signal in PC2. Peer R6 addresses broader morphospace patterns (C27-C31, C50, C53, C60, C61, C65) including PC2 results within the context of overall shape-change trends.

Minimal overlap on taxonomic patterns (C53). OpenEval supports specific taxonomic observations in morphospace plots. Peer R6 includes C53 within broader acknowledgment of shape-change trends and morphological variability findings.

Minimal overlap on morphological variation interpretation (C72). OpenEval supports the cautious interpretation linking lack of correlation to morphological variability. Peer R3 includes C72 within broader support for convergent evolution and biomechanical factors.

Minimal overlap on prior hypotheses (C14, C15). OpenEval supports these as appropriately cited background establishing knowledge gaps. Peer R1 includes these within broader acknowledgment of the study's contribution to understanding titanosaurian evolution.

OpenEval supports claims about clade composition and temporal ranges from cited literature (C55, C56, C93-C98). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature-based claims.
OpenEval supports specific anatomical observations with appropriate citations (C52, C67, C99, C100). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these detailed anatomical claims.

Minimal overlap on taxonomic patterns (C54). OpenEval supports morphospace observations for specific taxa. Peer R3 includes C54 within convergent evolution findings without detailed evaluation of individual taxonomic patterns.
